transport.shape: flat: every field sits alongside `type`, no envelope
transport.firstServerFrame: serverInfo, ahead of every reply; unsolicited activity broadcasts for sessions that already existed may precede it

create.notes: cols/rows omitted means the core picks its own spawn grid. Replies created + attached, or error.

input.notes: seq present means the core must reply with a matching inputAck; absent means no ack.

resize.notes: seq present means the core must reply with a matching resizeAck.

serverInfo.notes: Frame 0 on every connection. Nothing precedes it, not even the unsolicited activity broadcasts for sessions that were already live, so a client always knows the version and capability list before it has to interpret anything. See the SERVER_INFO_ORDERING rule. clientId is this connection's grid-ownership token, present on a core that advertises gridOwner: it is the value that comes back as the owner of gridChange and resizeAck when this connection holds the grid, and without it a client can see who drives the grid but not whether that is itself.

attached.notes: Also re-sent as a repaint when a stalled connection's output buffer overflowed.

screen.notes: reset: true carries every row; reset: false only the changed rows. Geometry or alt-buffer flips force a reset.

resizeAck.notes: applied: the grid reached a live pty. denied: another client owns the shared grid, so re-sending is futile. owner (gridOwner cores): who holds the grid after the arbitration, so a denied client learns who to wait for; string | null, always present as a key, null for an unclaimed grid and for the unarbitrated ephemeral editor/terminal ptys.

gridChange.notes: Broadcast to every connection whenever the arbitrated grid changes hands: a resize granted, or an owner letting go (its pane torn down, its connection closed). owner is string | null and is always present as a key; null means the grid is unclaimed again. Also sent once per already-owned session when a connection opens, so a client arriving mid-flight starts from the truth rather than assuming the grid is free. NOT sent for an unclaimed grid on connect: silence already means nobody is driving. resizeAck is the private answer to one client's request; this is the shared state.

exit.notes: exitCode is number | null and is always present as a key.

activity.notes: state is busy | idle | waiting_input. changes rides only the settle edge; both optionals are omitted, not null.

sessionMeta.notes: A session's persisted meta changed out of band: a title landing from the CLI-title poll or an OSC 0/2 window title, a rename, an archive or dormant flip. Carries the whole SessionMeta — replace the row wholesale, do not patch fields. created and attached remain the snapshot; this is the delta, so a client's session row is not frozen at whatever meta it attached with. Editor sessions are included, unlike activity: a meta edit is not a turn.

trackedPrs.notes: The whole watch list, replaced wholesale. Sent once in answer to subscribeTrackedPrs and after that only when the list changed. See TRACKED_PRS_ARE_CHANGES.

rules: An unrecognised client `type` is ignored, never fatal: a newer client must not be able to kill the connection.
Malformed JSON gets one error frame and the connection stays open.
A client feature-detects off serverInfo.capabilities and must refuse a core whose protocolVersion it does not implement.

SERVER_INFO_ORDERING: serverInfo is frame 0. Nothing may precede it: not a reply frame (created, attached, output, screen, inputAck, resizeAck, exit, queue, editorReady, terminalReady, unresumable, error, trackedPrs), and not an unsolicited activity broadcast either. A core must queue the handshake before it starts the activity fan-out, so a connection opened while other sessions are already live still reads serverInfo first and their activity after it.

TRACKED_PRS_ARE_CHANGES: a trackedPrs frame is the whole watch list, replaced wholesale, and it is a change notification. A core sends one snapshot in answer to subscribeTrackedPrs, and after that only when the list it would send differs from the one that connection was last sent. A poll pass that found nothing, or any other internal refresh that moved nothing, sends no frame at all: an identical list carries no information, and a redundant one races whatever the client asks for next, so a client that untracks a PR is answered by a snapshot that still lists it as watched.
A cursor-only change (show/hide, a move with no cell damage) is not guaranteed its own screen frame; it rides the next frame that carries damage.

A new server frame is additive within a protocol version: a client ignores a `type` it does not know, exactly as a core ignores an unknown client `type`. So gridChange and sessionMeta arrived in v1 without a version bump, gated by capability strings a client feature-detects rather than by a new version. A version bump is for a change that alters or removes what an existing frame already means.

decisions.childPid: Deliberately never on the wire. A pid from another process is not addressable, and from another machine it is meaningless. The one caller (the desktop's agent-worktree detection, which matches `git worktree list` output against the pty child's pid) degrades to no detection when a core answers nil, and falls back to the session cwd. If that detection has to work against a remote core, the operation moves core-side — the core knows both the pid and the cwd — and the answer surfaces as a SessionMeta field, so still no pid crosses the wire.
decisions.submit / insert: Core-side, not composed by the client. They are not `input` plus a delay: the core delivers a bracketed paste and verifies it landed against the session's headless VT model, retrying on the checks in between, and reports a PasteOutcome. A client reimplementing that needs the model, the retry timing and the failure taxonomy. The remote path is a client frame asking the core to run it, plus an outcome frame; neither exists yet.
decisions.autoSubmit: Core-side, same reasoning as submit, more strongly: it retries across the CLI's boot window until the input box exists. Today it is reachable over the wire only at create time, via create.initialInput, which cannot serve a session that already exists.
decisions.kickQueue: Core-side. The pending-message queue lives in the core and flushes on the idle edge; there is nothing for a client to compose. It needs a client frame of its own (the `queue` capability's fourth verb), which does not exist yet.
decisions.setTitle / setArchived / releaseGrid: Core-side operations with no client frame yet. A remote client can observe all three landing (sessionMeta, gridChange) but cannot cause them: a rename and an archive flip have no wire message and no REST route, and a grid release only happens when the owning connection closes. Filed rather than guessed at here.
